key_insight: Four AI trading agents showed high rule adherence, including an unprofitable agent, demonstrating that discipline alone does not establish profitability.
engineering_relevance: Agent-control systems should enforce explicit risk limits and audit rule adherence separately from financial performance before meaningful autonomy or capital allocation.
method: Evaluated four agents across a shared asset universe and execution conditions.
Required declared strategies, stops and targets, with a five-position limit per agent.
Audited trade logs for stop compliance, risk stability and position-limit exceptions.
evidence_signal: Across 2,627 closed positions, agents kept 97.5% of gross loss within declared stops, and 23 of 24 runs respected the position limit; 18% of positions involved real orders.
watch_item: Mostly simulated, trade-level results do not establish account-level returns or a lasting trading edge.
paper_title: The Control Layer Behind Rule-Following Agents Trading Across Market Conditions
